The Certificate manifest can be applied and reconciled before the PCA CA has its certificate associated and is ACTIVE. The CA certificate association is the operational prerequisite for issuing certificates; the current references only establish a dependency on the CA authority and issuer manifest, not on its activation.
This explicit dependency duplicates the node group's implicit dependency: its node_role_arn references the same IAM role, so Terraform already orders the node group after it.

The AWSPCAClusterIssuer custom resource is applied before this module is guaranteed to install the cert-manager and AWS PCA issuer charts/CRDs. Without waiting for the add-ons module, Kubernetes may reject the manifest because its custom resource definition is not yet registered.
The node group already has an implicit dependency on this role through its node_role_arn configuration, so the explicit depends_on edge duplicates it.
The trust-policy update command interpolates the role ID, which already creates an implicit dependency on the role; the explicit depends_on duplicates that edge.
The trust-policy update command interpolates the namespace ID, which already creates an implicit dependency on the namespace; the explicit depends_on duplicates that edge.
The autoscaling group depends on the launch-template outputs, whose configuration already depends on the instance profile. The explicit edge to the profile duplicates this transitive ordering.
The autoscaling group depends on the launch-template outputs, whose instance-profile dependency already orders it after the IAM role. The explicit role edge duplicates that transitive ordering.

The issuer manifest uses the PCA authority ARN while the authority is still in PENDING_CERTIFICATE until its certificate is associated. Ordering issuer creation after the authority-certificate association avoids configuring the issuer against a CA that cannot yet issue certificates.
